classification.difficultyReason: Apply the reciprocal transformation to an absolute-value graph, preserving symmetry and the corner at its maximum.

answer.short: A positive curve symmetric about the $y$-axis, with a corner maximum at $(0,1)$ and horizontal asymptote $y=0$. No $x$-intercepts or vertical asymptotes.
answer.worked: Sketch $f(x)=1+|x|$, a V-shaped graph with minimum $(0,1)$. The point $(0,1)$ remains unchanged under the reciprocal transformation. On either side, increasing $|x|$ increases $f(x)$, so its reciprocal decreases towards $0$. Join the two positive branches at $(0,1)$, retaining the corner. Since $f(x)\geq1$, there are no vertical asymptotes.

spec.description: Two positive branches meet at a corner on the y-axis at y=1 and approach the x-axis at both ends.
spec.mathematics: Exact piecewise plot of y=1/(1+|x|). Domain R; range (0,1]; corner maximum (0,1); horizontal asymptote y=0.
